resolutions.researcher_notes: No independent, citable source found for Capacity=12.00 bcm/y. The prior deep-sweep researcher found this exact figure (12 mlrd. m3/god) only in studfile.net, a banned tertiary re-upload host, so that source cannot be used. I re-searched in Russian ('Газли-Нукус газопровод 12 млрд куб м мощность', '"Газли-Нукус" 1220 мм 350 км', 'Zeromax "Газли-Нукус" газопровод 2004') and re-read the full text of every candidate document already on this row: caravan.kz (2004) states only the intermediate step -- the 2004 expansion raised capacity to 7 bcm/y -- and does not itself state the final 12 bcm/y figure; gazeta.uz (2016) and podrobno.uz (2016) describe only the new 74-75 km Gazli-Nukus<->Bukhara-Ural connector and give no capacity figure for the base line; AO Uztransgaz's own 2020 sustainability report (utg.uz PDF, checked in full via pdftotext -- see the Diameter/Owner units below) mentions Gazli-Nukus exactly once, in a pipe-diameter/reconstruction-scope context, with no capacity figure anywhere in the document. No second, non-blocklisted source states 12 bcm/y for this pipeline. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than reusing the banned host.

Resolves the deep-sweep's open spec caveat (it recommended 'checking a Uztransgaz/GIPRONIIgaz asset table if one surfaces'). AO 'Uztransgaz''s own 2020 Sustainable Development Report (title page: 'AO Uztransgaz | Otchet po ustoychivomu razvitiyu za 2020 god') lists, in its 2021-2023 reconstruction-programme scope: 'Magistralny gazoprovod "Gazli - Nukus" I nitka Du 1,220 mm uchastok 21-43 km, 167-188 km protyazhennostyu 43 km' -- 'Main gas pipeline "Gazli-Nukus", thread I, diameter (Du) 1,220 mm, sections km 21-43 and km 167-188, 43 km total' -- English gloss above. This is 'нитка I' (thread/string I, the physical pipe itself), not 'очередь' (construction phase/stage) -- different terminology from caravan.kz's 'первая очередь' (first phase). The km-post ranges (21-43 and 167-188) sit well inside the 350 km base corridor and are plainly the ORIGINAL 1997 line, not the later 66 km (2004) or 74-75 km (2016) add-on segments that the deep sweep already ruled out as diameter sources -- so this is the first source found that ties 1220 mm to the base line specifically. VERIFIER NOTE: url_verifier.py FAILs this URL on content ('200 but missing expected') -- this is the documented large-PDF false-negative (see the verifier's own docstring re: the OPEC ASB2012 case): the file is 16.0 MB / 15,030 pdftotext-extracted lines and the extractor does not reach page-deep content. Manually confirmed instead: curl -sI returns HTTP/2 200, content-type application/pdf, content-length 16780903 bytes; downloaded and ran pdftotext, and the exact sentence above appears verbatim at line 1410 of the extracted text. Single source (tier medium) -- searched for a second independent source (GulfPub, other Uztransgaz publications, press) without success; no source found gives a CONFLICTING diameter for the base line either.

Same document as the Diameter unit above (AO Uztransgaz's own 2020 Sustainable Development Report). It names 'Magistralny gazoprovod "Gazli - Nukus"' by name inside ITS OWN 2021-2023 network reconstruction programme, alongside its other trunk lines (Bukhara-Ural, Gazli-Kagan, DBST) -- i.e. Uztransgaz's own asset/investment document lists Gazli-Nukus as one of the pipelines it is planning to reconstruct, which is the company reporting on infrastructure under its own operational control. Caveat: the report does not use an explicit ownership formula ('Gazli-Nukus prinadlezhit AO Uztransgaz' / '100%'); it is inferred from the pipeline appearing by name inside the company's own network-investment scope, the same inferential basis the deep sweep already used to confirm Status=operating from context rather than a literal statement. This is the first source found that ties 'Gazli-Nukus' by NAME to Uztransgaz specifically -- the deep sweep's candidates (caravan.kz names the 1990s/2004 predecessor holding NKh Uzbekneftegaz, not Uztransgaz; gazligs.com names Uztransgaz's Gazli UMG branch but never mentions Gazli-Nukus by name) did not achieve this. Single source (tier medium) -- searched Russian press for a second explicit owner/operator statement without success. VERIFIER NOTE: same large-PDF url_verifier.py false-negative as the Diameter unit; manually confirmed live (HTTP 200) and content-present via pdftotext as described there. Note for the record: caravan.kz (2004) names the CUSTOMER/OWNER/OPERATOR of the pipeline's 2004 second-stage expansion as NHK 'Uzbekneftegaz' (Uztransgaz's parent/predecessor for gas transport at that date, per the deep sweep's own reasoning) -- this is an earlier-era holding-company name, not a disagreement with the current Owner1=Uztransgaz value, but flagging it since it is a differently-named entity.
